q2b.money_definition: A day's money = its ledger (energy + FCESS - wear; capacity, refunds, contracts are 0 on m1) + its calendar month's RT7 bill saving against the factory without a battery, per day (vpp.stochastic.daily_money). IRCR is not in it (see own_value).
q2b.source: analysis/2026-10-26/ui_redesign/export/site_summary_replay.py -> export/site_summary_replay_money.csv (current code, columns v1 and rw50+state t5+roll); published (old code): reports/v2_test_daily.csv + reports/v2_test_bills.csv via vpp.stochastic.daily_money, reproducing reports/v2_test_result.csv; interval: vpp.v2.backtest.month_ci
q2b.note: Current code differs from the published outputs on: e5 ['2025-12-05', '2025-12-08', '2026-02-02'], v1 ['2025-12-05', '2025-12-08', '2026-02-02'] (both were over 10 MW there before the 2026-10-26 fix). On those days v1 gains more than e5, so the in-sample uplift is a little lower than the published reports (see published_old_code); on 2026-10-26 reports/v2_test_*.csv and findings.md section 27 were regenerated with the fixed code and now equal these values. The test's seen / unseen split is reported by the repo for the means (reports/v2_test_result.csv rows 'test to 2026-10-15' and 'test from 2026-10-16'); p10, share and worst day are computed here from the daily money. Bill savings are monthly and spread over the month's days, so the unseen segment shares October's bill with the seen one. 2026-10-22 has no 'tomorrow' yet and changes at the next data refresh (findings.md 27.5).

q2a.metric: MAE, A$/MWh (energy price, half-hours 09:00-07:30 of each trading day)
q2a.baseline: yesterday's price (same half-hour of the previous trading day, yday_energy)
q2a.forecast: strict 09:00 same-day forecast the dispatcher uses: 50/50 blend of (AEMO pre-dispatch + ML correction + weather) and (ML + weather, no AEMO), walk-forward monthly refits, trained on data to 2026-06-30 at most (vpp/forecast.py)

derived.change_pct: 100 * (model - baseline) / baseline (negative = smaller error than the baseline)

q2a.source: data/processed/forecast_dispatch_0900.parquet columns energy, yday_energy, actual_energy, target_date; the same computation as vpp/forecast.py main(), split by period. Reproduces findings.md:754 (test 07-01..10-15: 19.66 vs 28.79) and findings.md:879 (in-sample point MAE 20.12).
q2a.note: The repo reports the in-sample model MAE and the test-seen pair; the in-sample baseline and the test-unseen pair are computed here. Not an accuracy: a lower MAE is a smaller average error in A$/MWh.

periods.note: Counts of half-hours (e5, current code) over: battery power 10 MW (|energy_mwh| / 0.5 h, vpp/checks.py I11), stored energy outside 0-40 MWh (I3), meter import 12 MW and export 10 MW (I1). CMD 9 MW is an economic limit priced in the RT7 bill (excess network use charge on the month's highest half-hour), not a hard limit; the dispatcher's cap is max(CMD, the month-to-date peak) (vpp/v2/harness.py:207), so once a month has gone above the CMD, later half-hours up to that peak add no charge. Meter above the CMD in 627 half-hours on 147 days (578 by more than 0.01 MW, 207 by more than 0.1 MW); months whose bill peak is above the CMD: 2025-04 9.621 MW, 2025-05 9.167 MW, 2025-06 9.290 MW, 2025-07 9.060 MW, 2025-08 9.059 MW, 2025-09 9.282 MW, 2025-10 9.121 MW, 2025-11 9.074 MW, 2026-01 9.032 MW, 2026-04 9.033 MW, 2026-06 9.115 MW, excess charge in those months A$26,308 (in the money above)

hard_limits.power_cap_note: Results made before the 2026-10-26 fix (analysis/2026-10-26/power_cap_fix): e5 was over 10 MW on 3 in-sample days (2025-12-05, 2025-12-08, 2026-02-02, 17:00-17:30, up to 10.50 MW; 3 half-hours); fixed code: 0 on every day. Money effect on e5 in-sample +A$0.02/day, test 0. The v1 baseline was also over 10 MW in the published outputs (3 half-hours on 2025-12-05, 2025-12-08, 2026-02-02); with the fixed code it is 0 and v1 earns +A$1.32/day more in-sample, so the in-sample uplift is 406.86 (published 408.16). Test periods unchanged.
